football_evidence.question: Can Florida State’s pass rush get to Mason McKenzie?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Boston College, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.3 of the 2.5 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Boston College has the ball (big plays on the ground): Boston College’s offense turns 10.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and Florida State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.8% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Florida State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Florida State’s offense has allowed a sack on 9.0% of its dropbacks, and Boston College’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Boston College has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Boston College’s offense averages 5.9 yards per carry, and Florida State’s defense allows 6.2 yards per carry (FBS average 5.0).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Boston College’s run defense No. 55 nationally and Florida State’s No. 92.
contradicting: When Boston College has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Boston College’s offense has allowed a sack on 9.8% of its dropbacks, and Florida State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Florida State has the ball (big plays through the air): Florida State’s offense turns 16.6% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Boston College’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.4% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Florida State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Florida State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 10.5% of its runs, and Boston College’s defense stops 18.3% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
In his last two games (Georgia Tech and Duke), McKenzie averaged 5.0 yards per attempt, against 7.7 in his six games before that.
quarterbacks: Mason McKenzie has completed 116 of 200 passes (58.0%) for 1,452 yards, 7.3 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 7 interceptions in eight games for Boston College, and has been sacked on 21 of 221 dropbacks.

Ashton Daniels has completed 127 of 218 passes (58.3%) for 1,966 yards, 9.0 yards per attempt, 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in eight games for Florida State, and has been sacked on 21 of 239 dropbacks.
